issue: The text says a leaf certificate is checked in time polynomial in its encoding length. Def. def:leaf allows any finite family of polytopes whose union is Pi, and checking that union is coNP-hard in k. DNF tautology reduces to it: map each term to the box with [1/2,1] for a positive literal, [0,1/2] for a negated one and [0,1] otherwise. An arrangement-based check costs (Rm)^{O(p)}, which is neither poly(I) nor f(p)poly(I). Theorem cv(i) therefore claims more than holds.
fix: In Def. def:leaf require 'a rational binary space partition of Pi (each internal node splits its polytope by one rational hyperplane into two closed halves with nonempty interiors) whose leaves P_1..P_R each carry a certificate'. Drop the conditional 'When the leaves are produced by a binary space partition' (l.79). Prop cert-exist already produces such certificates, and Lemma cv-bits already descends the partition tree.

issue: The acceptance test accepts z~ when its lifted value equals the unique rational of denominator at most Omega_0 in [beta,U]. That is correct only if OPT has denominator at most Omega_0. Lemma cv-height proves this only for a unique minimizer, yet l.406-407 claims 'An accepted point is feasible with optimal value, hence optimal, independently of growth.' Without uniqueness, the claimed validity has no proof.
fix: Restate the lemma: 'Some global minimizer x* of f on P has x*=w/q with 1<=q<=Lambda_0 (the unique one if it is unique); hence OPT has denominator <= 2D_f Lambda_0^2.' In the proof, choose a global minimizer whose active set E has maximal cardinality. If some nonzero d in T had Hd orthogonal to T, then d^T H d=0 and f would be constant on x*+td; moving until a new row becomes active (P is bounded) would enlarge the active set. So the reduced Hessian is nonsingular and PSD, hence PD, and the saddle-matrix argument applies unchanged.
